name: Brown & Brown, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate moat: recurring renewal commissions, carrier scale and contingent-commission leverage, and a proven decentralized M&A platform — but it is a people business with low formal switching costs (departed producers took ~$31M of annualized revenue to a startup competitor), cyclical P&C pricing exposure, larger rivals (Marsh McLennan, Aon, Gallagher), and growth that depends on continuous debt/equity-funded acquisitions rather than organic compounding (organic growth 2.8% in 2025, -0.3% ex-contingents in H1 2026).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 3.9%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Quality insurance-brokerage roll-up, moat 5/10 — but at $67.98 it does not clear 15% on filing-derived TTM numbers (weighted IRR 10.5%, IV@15 $42.63); the historical growth in the filings is bought, not organic, and the Accession debt load stresses the bear cases. Clears 15% at ~$42.63.
moat_for: Recurring renewal commission base with high client retention
Carrier scale and contingent (profit-sharing) commission leverage
Proven decentralized acquisition platform, decades-long track record
Asset-light model — minimal capex, strong cash conversion
moat_against: People business: producers can leave and take accounts (startup competitor took ~$31M annualized revenue; litigation ongoing)
Low formal switching costs for clients
Organic growth stalling: 2.8% in 2025, -0.3% ex-contingents in H1 2026; soft P&C pricing, cat-property rate declines
Growth depends on continuous M&A funded with debt and equity issuance
Accession integration risk and margin dilution; interest expense roughly doubled YoY in Q2 2026
